newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs' new state airline starts flying March 8.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs' new state airline starts flying March 8.

text.p: Air Kazakstan, the former Soviet republic's new state-owned airline, will start flying domestic routes from March 8, state television said on Thursday.
The new airline plans to start international services at a later date, the Khabar evening news programme said, but did not say when.
Air Kazakstan replaces Kazakhstan National Airways, or KazAir, one of the myriad "baby-flots" carved out of Aeroflot after the Soviet collapse in 1991.
The airline was formally closed down last August after running up $149 million worth of debts, but continued operating for a few months.
KazAir also lost an Ilyushin Il-76 cargo plane in the catastrophic mid-air collision with a Saudi Boeing 747 over the Indian capital Delhi last November, with a loss of some 350 lives.
The president of the new company, Rustam Bekturov, told the programme that the airline would have to increase fares to meet rising service costs at Almaty's airport.
